title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on p.111 Grothendieck defines an 'atelier' (workshop) as a structure (𝓕, ≤, ≪ ; |o|). Here 𝓕 is a set of 'figures' with a partial order ≤ (containment), a second relation ≪ (read as 'well inside' or 'relatively compact in'), and a relation |o|.

Axioms on p.111:
- At1: 𝓕 is nonempty and every ≤-bounded family has a supremum.
- At2: every figure F is the supremum of its 'structure' F~ = {X ≤ F, X strictly irreducible}.
- M denotes the set of elementary (strictly irreducible) figures.
- The (𝓕, ≤) part is then equivalent to (M, ≤) together with a family 𝓕~ of downward-closed subsets of M (the F~), under F ↦ F~. In this correspondence F ≤ G ⇔ F~ ⊂ G~ and sup corresponds to union. This is a Birkhoff-type representation by completely join-prime elements.

This page completes the axiom list.
- At4: F ≪ G ⇔ ∀X∈F~ ∃Y∈G~ with X ≪ Y. So ≪ on 𝓕 is determined by its restriction to M.
- At3 (rewritten). (a) For F, G in 𝓕, the join F∨G exists iff every X ∈ F~∖(F~∩G~) and every Y ∈ G~∖(F~∩G~) satisfy X |o| Y. So |o| acts as a binary compatibility (coherence) relation that controls when two figures have a union. (b) F |o| G implies F, G ∈ M, so |o| is really a relation on M. A crossed-out At5 said the same thing.
- Add axioms Mag1–Mag4, not given here, on the quadruple (M, ≤, ≪, |o|).
- Variant formulation: giving an atelier is the same as giving 𝓕~ ⊂ 𝔓(M) such that:
  - AtM1: each Φ ∈ 𝓕~ is ≤-closed, i.e. a lower set.
  - AtM2: 𝓕~ is stable under passing to closed subsets.
  - AtM3: the members of 𝓕~ cover M and 𝓕~ ≠ ∅ (equivalently ∅ ∈ 𝓕~).
  - AtM4 (next page): Φ∪Ψ ∈ 𝓕~ iff the elements are pairwise compatible.
- Next page, finite case: if each X~ is finite, then 𝓕~ is exactly the finite lower sets of M that are pairwise non-conflicting.

Modern reading. (M, ≤, conflict) with finite-cause axiom 'Mag fin' and binary consistency is a prime event structure (Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981). 𝓕~ is its family of configurations, and the atelier (𝓕, ≤) is the associated coherent prime-algebraic domain (dI-domain). When ≤ is discrete one gets Girard's coherence spaces (1986–87). The problem served is a combinatorial-axiomatic foundation for 'analysis situs' (tame topology). Figures are presented as consistent unions of elementary pieces, with ≪ playing the role of a 'well-inside' relation.
errors: At3 states the binary compatibility criterion only for pairs F, G. The representation of arbitrary bounded sups (At1) by unions needs either an infinitary version or an explicit coherence axiom: pairwise-joinable families are joinable. This is not stated here, though AtM4 on the next page is again only binary.
For the equivalence 𝓕 ≅ 𝓕~ with sup = union, 'strictly irreducible' must mean completely join-prime, not merely join-irreducible. The notes do not make this explicit.

Whether |o| denotes compatibility or its negation (conflict) is ambiguous. On the next page Grothendieck rewrites the condition via X≉Y, defined through |o| on the parts X~∖(X~∩Y~), so the primitive relation and the derived one differ. The convention is not fixed on this page.

At4 transfers ≪ from M to 𝓕, but transitivity and compatibility of ≪ with ≤ on 𝓕 are presumably delegated to Mag1–4 (not visible). Nothing on the page checks that the induced relation is again of the required type.

ideas.what: Representation of a poset of figures by downward-closed sets of strictly irreducible elements, sup = union (At1, At2, AtM1–3)
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff-type representation via completely join-prime elements; prime-algebraic domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937, finite distributive lattices); Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981, prime algebraic domains)

ideas.what: Existence of F∨G characterized by a binary relation |o| on the elementary pieces not shared by F and G (At3a, AtM4)
ideas.modern_name: binary consistency / conflict relation; coherent domains; configurations of prime event structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981 (event structures); Plotkin (coherent domains); Girard 1986–87 (coherence spaces)

ideas.what: Extension of the 'well-inside' relation ≪ from elementary figures to all figures by the ∀∃ rule (At4)
ideas.modern_name: lifting a relation to lower sets (Egli–Milner/Hoare-type lifting); relation generating an auxiliary order as in way-below/proximity structures

ideas.what: Atelier with finite figures: 𝓕~ = finite pairwise-compatible lower sets, under the axiom that each X~ is finite (next page, 'Mag fin')
ideas.modern_name: finite configurations of an event structure with finite causes

missed.claim: In his 1986 tame-topology 'atelier' axioms, Grothendieck independently arrives at what are essentially prime event structures with binary conflict and their configuration domains (coherent prime-algebraic domains). This is a semantics notion from theoretical computer science. The equivalence atelier ⇔ (M, ≤, |o|, 𝓕~) mirrors the Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel representation theorem. The link between Grothendieck's combinatorial analysis situs and domain theory / event structures / Girard's coherence spaces (contemporaneous, 1986–87) appears not to have been made in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour que {F,G} ... i.e. F∨G existe, il faut et il suffit que ∀X ∈ F~∖F~∩G~, Y ∈ G~∖F~∩G~ ⇒ X|o|Y ... |o| est en fait une relation dans M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests reading tame/combinatorial geometry ('figures' built from elementary cells with a conflict/compatibility relation and a well-inside relation ≪) through domain theory and event structures, which already has mature tools. Conversely, Grothendieck's extra ≪ data and the unseen Mag axioms may give a geometric enrichment of event structures.

missed.claim: The axioms Mag1–Mag4 on (M, ≤, ≪, |o|) are invoked but not written on this page. The atelier/M-atelier equivalence is sketched but not proved, including the infinitary coherence gap.
missed.quote: + les axiomes Mag 1 – Mag 4 sur les (M, ≤, ≪, |o|)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A completed version would be an explicit axiomatics of 'figures' for Grothendieck's tame topology programme (Esquisse §5) that is not in the published record.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically elementary order theory. However, it is a clear, dated instance of Grothendieck formulating, for analysis situs, a structure equivalent to event structures and coherent domains, apparently unconnected in the literature. It is a notable unpublished detail rather than a deep result.
transcription_corrections: The underlined word in 'la donnée d'une atlas' is 'atelier' (as on p.111), not 'atlas'. The sentence reads roughly 'la donnée d'un atelier (variante) ⇔ la donnée de 𝓕~ ⊂ 𝔓(M) satisfaisant les conditions'.
'(spéc.)' is written under the crossed-out At5, likely '(spécial)'. It qualifies the rewritten At3 / is a marginal tag, not part of the formula.
In At3(a), 'admette sup dans F~^≤' likely reads 'soit majoré dans 𝓕^≤', i.e. {F,G} bounded in (𝓕,≤), whence F∨G exists. The ambient set is 𝓕, not F~.

Left-margin notes are very uncertain. The lower one plausibly reads 'Condition de compatibilité pour structures' rather than 'réversibilité'. The upper one is illegible ('Condition de ... avec ...'); 'Antho' is doubtful.

'En termes de cette donnée structure [?]' likely reads 'En termes de cette structure ...' followed by an underlined/overwritten word ('associations ...'). The reading 'association magique' is doubtful.
